audit_drops.reason: Twin leftover: 'The customer asked whether the refund covers postage' survives from the gold-1 twin (427, 'We side with the customer; refund'). In the gold-0 row it presupposes a refund was granted, so the row can be read as stating the outcome.

Client's own recollection ('You told me yesterday you have taken this on, so it is all settled') of a verbal statement. It can be read as a settled-outcome claim (gold) or as a party's assertion/request about an intake that is still open. Solver flagged it too (0.7). Two readings are defensible; dropped for consistency with planted_a party-claim drops.

audit_notes: Read all 750 rows (every module: cm, is, lg, lo, hb, mp, ps), including both twins of every pair; re-checked every rule-application arithmetic item (e.g. 18, 60, 247, 281, 313, 358, 365, 393, 402, 438, 459, 528, 574, 680, 704, 724, 728, 744): all consistent.
Solver-flagged ids 12, 163, 248, 289, 594 kept: gold follows the card literally (claim of settlement / sign-off of this case; paralegal opinion is not a decision).

Distribution bias (not a per-row flaw): in 310 of 375 twin pairs the gold-1 twin is the longer one (X-type twins append the dictating sentence); single-row length vs gold AUC 0.64. Cue words skew to gold 1 (decided 25/2, close 16/1, final 55/9, approved 33/6) but gold-0 counterexamples exist (e.g. 21, 433, 561, 667).
